samples.text:
The diagram illustrate the life cycle of the honeybee. It have six stages and it is a cycle.

At the beginning, the queen lays an egg in a wax cell. After 3 days the egg hatches and becomes a larva. The larva is fed royal jelly at first and then pollen and honey, and this stage is 6 days. Then the worker bees seal the cell with a wax.

After that the larva is a pupa. In this stage it develop legs, wings and eyes, and it takes about 12 days. On day 21 the adult bee chews through the wax cap and comes out of the cell.

Finally, the adult becomes a worker bee. The worker bee cleans, feeds larvae and later it collects nectar. It lives for 5–6 weeks. Then the cycle start again with a new egg from the queen.

Overall, the honeybee has six stages from egg to worker bee, and the development inside the cell take 21 days in total, which is much shorter than the life of the worker bee.
samples.why: Overview placed late and basic · all stages and timings covered in order · repetitive linking · adequate but plain vocabulary · several agreement and article errors that do not affect understanding.

samples.text:
The diagram shows the various stages in the life of a honeybee, from the moment an egg is laid until the bee becomes a working member of the colony.

Overall, the life cycle consists of six stages and is cyclical. It takes 21 days for an egg to develop into an adult, while the adult worker bee lives for only a few weeks.

The cycle begins when the queen lays an egg in a wax cell. After three days, the egg hatches into a larva, which is fed on royal jelly at first and later on pollen and honey for a period of six days. At the end of this stage, worker bees seal the cell with wax.

Inside the capped cell, the larva develops into a pupa, growing legs, wings and eyes over approximately 12 days. On day 21, the adult bee emerges by chewing through the wax cap. It then becomes a worker bee, which cleans, feeds larvae and eventually collect nectar. Worker bees live for five to six weeks, and new eggs laid by the queen continue the cycle.
samples.why: Clear overview with the key timing · stages logically sequenced with good cohesion · some less common vocabulary (emerges, capped cell) · frequent error-free sentences with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
The diagram charts the development of the honeybee through the six stages of its life cycle, which begins with an egg and ends with a mature worker bee.

It is evident that the entire transformation from egg to adult is completed within 21 days, much of it inside a sealed wax cell, whereas the adult worker survives for just five to six weeks before the cycle begins anew with fresh eggs.

Initially, the queen deposits an egg in a wax cell, and three days later this hatches into a larva. For the following six days, the larva is fed first on royal jelly and subsequently on pollen and honey, after which worker bees cap the cell with wax.

Sealed within, the insect enters the pupal stage, lasting about 12 days, during which it develops legs, wings and eyes. On day 21, the fully formed adult chews its way out through the wax cap. It then takes on the role of a worker bee, initially cleaning and feeding larvae before progressing to collecting nectar. As new eggs are laid by the queen, the cycle is repeated continuously.
samples.why: Well-judged overview contrasting development time and adult lifespan · timings selected accurately · cohesion managed seamlessly · precise vocabulary (deposits, pupal stage) · varied complex structures · error-free.
